_comment: Adjoint backward linear solver: transposed CPR (cprt) with hypre BoomerAMG as the pressure/coarse solve. Use via --adjoint-linear-solver=<this file>. cprt applies the CPR two-stage preconditioner to the TRANSPOSED reservoir system (the adjoint canonical form); the coarse (pressure) level is solved by hypre AMG, intended to scale to field size where umfpack's direct factors blow up in memory (SPE9: umfpack backward 4 GB vs iterative ~0.35 GB). BUILD: hypre is registered here (USE_HYPRE=ON + USE_MPI=ON; the opm-adjoint CMakeLists links HYPRE::HYPRE PUBLIC so HAVE_HYPRE reaches flow_adjoint; the HyprePreconditioner symbol is in the binary and this config runs). TOLERANCE: the outer 'tol' MUST be tight (1e-14, matching the default adjoint reduction) — a loose outer tol (the earlier 1e-2) makes the backward solve stop early and produced ~38% gradient error vs umfpack; do not loosen it. STATUS (measured 2026-07, this machine): at the scales reachable here hypre BoomerAMG does NOT beat the built-in dune-istl AMG coarse of the default 'cprt' preset — on SPE9 (9k) it is ~15% slower, and on Norne (44k, transposed system) it fails to converge to 1e-14 (stalls ~5e-9 in 300 iters) and aborts. So this is NOT the default; the auto/cprt path wins at <=44k. hypre only becomes worthwhile with (a) a >=1e5-cell case and (b) BoomerAMG options tuned for the transposed adjoint system (strong-threshold/coarsening/relaxation). For a working json-based coarse solve now, change coarsesolver.preconditioner.type from 'hypre' to 'amg' (converges, but still slower than the plain 'cprt' preset).
